title: Check yourself: Server-sent events, websockets and connection basics

questions.stem: A team's report generator sets a very large `max_tokens` on a non-streaming call and now fails intermittently on the office network after several minutes without any reply. Which change is best?

options.text: Open a websocket so that the server can push the report when it is ready
options.says: Ruled out because "there is no client-to-server traffic to carry" in a model call, and a websocket is "not what the API sends".

options.text: Turn on server-sent events so that data keeps flowing while the long text is produced
options.says: Streaming keeps data moving: "Bytes keep flowing, and the connection is not idle".

options.text: Raise the client timeout so that the call may stay silent for longer
options.says: Ruled out because "Some networks may drop idle connections after a variable period of time", so a longer timeout on your side does not help.

options.text: Split the report into three prompts and send them over three connections
options.says: Ruled out because "the call is silent for as long as the generation takes", and each of three connections would be silent while its own part is written.

questions.stem: A developer proposes a websocket between a web page and the model API so that the page can send a stop signal during a long answer. What does the page say is the better design?

options.text: Add a second HTTP request that tells the model to stop generating
options.says: Ruled out because the page documents "breaking out of the loop or calling stream.controller.abort()", not a second request.

options.text: Keep the single HTTP request and poll it every second for the next words
options.says: Ruled out because "the server answers with a normal HTTP response whose body is a stream of server-sent events", so the words arrive without polling.

options.text: Switch to the websocket, because only that protocol allows a cancel
options.says: Ruled out because "a websocket adds an upgrade, a session to restore and trouble at every proxy, and gives nothing in return".

options.text: Keep the single HTTP request and stream, and cancel by closing the connection
options.says: The page says the client cancels "by closing the connection", with the stream running on one ordinary HTTP request.
